Pentagon leaders warn that more marine vessels might experience coronavirus outbreaks, following an incident on a Pacific carrier where over 400 sailors were infected. General John Hyten, Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, announced today that a crew member from the USS Theodore Roosevelt is currently in intensive care on Guam. The ship has been docked there for over a week. Presently, 416 crew members are infected, and 1,164 test results are still pending.

"It's not wise to think that the situation with the Teddy Roosevelt is unique," Hyten stated at a Pentagon news conference. "We have numerous ships at sea... assuming it won't happen again is poor planning."

Admiral Mike Gilday highlighted the primary issue: the difficulty in conducting rapid and widespread testing, including for those aboard the USS Nimitz, the next U.S.-based carrier slated to deploy.

"The challenge we face is developing the capability to test in both volume and speed," Gilday informed a small group of reporters. "I can't provide a precise estimate on when we'll achieve the testing capacity we desire."

Sailors on the USS Nimitz, currently in port, will undergo a two-week quarantine before deployment. Although a civilian worker was transported to the Nimitz over a week ago after exhibiting symptoms, the test results were inconclusive. Hyten mentioned a small number of sick sailors, but the Navy clarified today that no current sailors on the Nimitz have tested positive for COVID-19 or displayed symptoms.

Retired Admiral James Stavridis, a former NATO commander, foresees continued challenges for the Navy and other military branches. "It's evident there are more challenges ahead," Stavridis expressed via email. "The Navy and all services face difficult decisions on whether to pull units to ensure their well-being or accept a certain level of risk due to the virus. I anticipate a case-by-case approach based on mission requirements."

Gilday noted that the Navy has learned from the Roosevelt outbreak, particularly the transition from prevention to managing the virus as sailors begin to show symptoms. As of today, 3,190 crew members have tested negative, with pending results for the remainder. About 2,700 sailors have been moved off the ship and accommodated at the base and hotels on the island. Those testing positive are monitored medically twice a day.

More broadly, Hyten stated that the Roosevelt incident illustrates how the military must adapt. "This will be a new operational reality we must address," he said, referencing the challenges of recruiting, training, deploying, and potentially engaging in combat during the pandemic. "We're adjusting to this new world in real time."

The outbreak on the Roosevelt began in late March, plunging the Navy into a leadership crisis. Thomas Modly resigned as Navy Secretary after dismissing Captain Brett E. Crozier, the Roosevelt's commander, for widely disseminating a letter urging the Navy to take swifter action to protect his crew. Modly faced backlash for visiting the Roosevelt and delivering remarks harshly critical of Crozier.

Gilday announced that the investigation into the Roosevelt incident, initiated last week, is complete, and he is reviewing the report. He has not ruled out any actions, including potentially reinstating Crozier, depending on the findings. The central issue is why Crozier felt the need to send the memo and whether it indicated a breakdown in communication and leadership. "All options are on the table," Gilday said regarding Crozier's future. He added that he hasn't spoken with Crozier and feels no external pressure concerning the investigation, emphasizing fairness in his actions.

In a separate appearance, General Mark Milley, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, remarked that despite the outbreak, the Roosevelt could be reactivated and return to duty if global events necessitate it. Speaking alongside Hyten, Deputy Secretary of Defense David Norquist emphasized that military leaders recognize the coronavirus as a long-term challenge. "We need to adapt, as the virus won't disappear in the coming months," Norquist stated. "We must learn to operate effectively in a COVID environment."

The new coronavirus generally causes mild or moderate symptoms, such as fever and cough, lasting two to three weeks. However, it can lead to severe illness, including pneumonia and death, particularly in older adults and those with pre-existing health conditions.

**Big Health's Daylight App Proven Effective for Generalized Anxiety Disorder in Randomized Controlled Trial**

**SAN FRANCISCO & LONDON – July 29, 2020 –** Big Health, the global leader in digital therapeutics for mental health, and the University of Oxford's Sleep Circadian Neuroscience Institute today announced the publication of a randomized controlled trial (RCT) in the journal *Depression and Anxiety*.  The study demonstrates the efficacy and safety of Big Health's Daylight app in improving symptoms of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).

The fully automated smartphone-based program leverages evidence-based cognitive and behavioral techniques to help users manage worry and anxiety.  Trial results revealed that Daylight significantly reduced anxiety symptoms compared to the control group after six weeks.  Impressively, 71% of Daylight users achieved remission of GAD by week 10, compared to just 33% in the control group.  These improvements were maintained even at the 26-week (uncontrolled) follow-up, which coincided with the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic – a period of heightened anxiety globally.

"This trial confirms that Daylight is a safe, effective first-line digital therapeutic for worry and anxiety," said Professor Jasper Smits, PhD, Department of Psychiatry at the University of Texas, Austin.  "The consistent and measurable improvements in mental health observed in Daylight users are significant and meaningful, demonstrating the potential of this software to offer relief to those suffering from worry, anxiety, and related conditions."

Anxiety is the most prevalent mental health issue in the United States, affecting over 40 million adults annually.  GAD, characterized by excessive and difficult-to-control worry accompanied by physical symptoms and functional impairment, affects 5-6% of the population in the UK and US, respectively. The COVID-19 pandemic has further exacerbated these challenges, with numerous surveys reporting increased rates of anxiety and stress.

"Anxiety and other mental health challenges cause immense distress globally, yet access to effective solutions remains limited due to stigma and the constraints of in-person care, further compounded by the pandemic," explained Dr. Jenna Carl, vice president of clinical development and medical affairs at Big Health. "These study results confirm Daylight's meaningful impact and its potential to support millions in achieving better mental health, particularly those with limited access to traditional care."

The trial involved 256 participants randomized to either the Daylight intervention or a control group (who received the intervention later).  Participants met criteria for GAD with moderate to severe symptoms, assessed using established clinical measures (MINI and SCID for diagnosis; GAD-7 for severity). Assessments occurred at baseline, mid-intervention (week 3), post-intervention (week 6, primary endpoint), follow-up (week 10), and long-term follow-up (week 26).

In addition to quantitative results, qualitative feedback from participants was positive, highlighting the app's engaging design, soothing voice guidance, practical tools, and overall effectiveness in managing anxiety.  Participants reported feeling more in control, better equipped to challenge negative thoughts, and more confident in their ability to handle anxiety.

Beyond the primary outcomes on anxiety, the study also found statistically significant improvements in worry, depressive symptoms, sleep difficulty, wellbeing, and quality of life.  The effects of Daylight were consistent across demographic groups and severity levels.

Daylight was developed in collaboration with anxiety experts from Boston University, UCLA, University of Oxford, and the University of Texas at Austin.  The program combines animation, developed by veterans of Pixar and Radiolab, with a calming human voice to create an immersive and personalized experience.  Daylight is Big Health's second digital therapeutic, following the success of Sleepio, its digital sleep improvement program.  Daylight has received CE mark approval, signifying its compliance with EU medical device safety and performance requirements.

Denver (CNN) — Colorado authorities have issued a warrant for homicide following the discovery of human remains in rural southern Colorado, police reported on Wednesday. Local and state officials announced that they uncovered the remains of three individuals on two properties in Lasauses, Colorado, while executing a search warrant.

Authorities are now seeking Adre Jordan Baroz, 26, in connection with these remains. "Our primary objective is to remove him from the streets," stated Alamosa Police Chief Ken Anderson, who announced the warrant. "He currently poses a danger to the public."

Chief Anderson also noted that Baroz is considered armed and dangerous. Lasauses is a small town situated along the Rio Grande in southern Colorado, nestled between Alamosa to the north and the New Mexico border to the south.

The investigators mentioned that the remains have yet to be identified. It may take weeks or even months to determine the gender, age, and identity of the deceased. However, Monte Vista Police Chief George Dingfelder confirmed that forensic anthropologists have established the remains belong to three individuals.

On November 10, the Conejos County Sheriff’s Office, which has jurisdiction in Lasauses, requested assistance from the Colorado Bureau of Investigation in executing the search warrant, according to Sheriff Garth Crowther. Upon discovering remains at the initial property, evidence prompted the authorities to search a nearby location, where they found additional remains.

Due to the ongoing investigation, law enforcement has not disclosed details regarding why Baroz has been identified as a suspect, how long the remains were on the properties, or whether they are connected to any recent missing persons cases. Investigators continue to search the properties for more remains and evidence.

CNN’s Eliott C. McLaughlin contributed to this report.

After Derby County's Championship play-off final loss to Aston Villa, a disheartened Tom Huddlestone was left pondering what could have been. "We have been in more challenging situations before – like Norwich away and Leeds in the play-offs. Everyone counted us out then, but we fought back. Towards the end, they appeared fatigued."

The Pegulas earned league-wide praise for how they operated the team, providing players access to the Sabres' practice and workout facilities, and assisting in marketing efforts. Without the Pegulas, the NWHL will need to cover the Beauts' operating and salary costs, estimated to be close to $200,000.

Last week, more than 200 players announced they would not play in North America this year without what they deem a single, economically viable professional league for women. The list included many Beauts players, such as U.S. national team defenseman Emily Pfalzer and Canadian national team goalie Shannon Szabados.

What have the national anthem, breastfeeding, sarcasm and environmental disasters got in common? Over the last year, there have been calls for each of these topics to be taught in schools – a practice known as ‘curriculum dumping’. Every time a societal issue arises, the expectation is for schools to address it.  If only pupils learned about knife crime, acid attacks, revenge porn, or gambling, the logic goes, these problems would disappear.

This raises some common sense questions. With an already packed curriculum, do schools have the time and expertise?  A new report by the campaign group Parents and Teachers for Excellence highlights this issue. After scouring social media, newspapers, and other sources, the group unearthed 213 examples of suggested new ‘subjects’ for 2018 alone.  It points out that schools would need hundreds of additional hours to teach them all.  The top three themes proposed were health, finance, and technology.  Other suggestions included the Commonwealth, workers’ rights, litter picking, the RAF, marriage, how to avoid dog bites, oceans, feminism, and even using trampolining to teach literacy skills or Love Island to critique celebrity culture.  Some of the more outlandish ideas included teaching sado-masochism and swearing.

The report also raises concerns over schools becoming ‘catnip’ for lobby groups and policy-makers, asking, “What should schools stop doing to make time for your proposal?” Parents and Teachers for Excellence concludes: “We believe that teachers and schools are the ones best placed to decide what their students need to know.”

Yet, sometimes policy-makers do offer valuable suggestions.  Education Secretary Damian Hinds recently revealed a new initiative: a ‘bucket list’ or ‘passport’ of activities for primary pupils, encouraging learning outside the classroom.  This recognizes that learning doesn’t have to be confined to school and that parents can be the natural educators.  The passport includes 20 activities for each year group.  Tasks for reception pupils include visiting a farm, painting a self-portrait, making a paper boat, re-telling a story to an audience, and posting a letter.

## Stuffed Oats Chilla
A health-conscious twist on traditional chilla, made with oat flour and vegetable stuffing. Perfect for breakfast, a wholesome snack, or main course.

### Ingredients
For the Chilla:
- 1 cup oats (powdered)
- 2 tbsp gram flour (besan)
- 1½ tsp oil
- ½ tsp chopped green chilies
- 1 cup water
- ½ tsp turmeric powder (haldi)
- ½ tsp asafetida (hing)
- 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves
- Salt to taste
- 3 tsp oil for cooking

For the Vegetable Stuffing:
- ½ cup boiled green peas
- ½ cup boiled potatoes, peeled & chopped
- ½ tbsp oil
- 1 tbsp chopped onions
- 1 tbsp chopped tomatoes
- ½ tsp turmeric powder
- ½ tsp garam masala
- Pinch of asafetida
- Salt and chili powder to taste
- 1 cup tamarind chutney for serving

### Method
1. **For the Stuffing:**
   - Heat oil in a vessel
   - Add turmeric powder, garam masala, asafetida, onions, and tomatoes; sauté for 30 seconds
   - Add green peas, potatoes, salt, and chili powder; cook for 2 minutes

2. **For the Chilla:**
   - Combine gram flour, green chilies, asafetida, coriander, turmeric powder, powdered oats, oil, water, and salt

**Spinach and Barley Risotto**

Serves 4 to 6.

**Ingredients:**

- 2 tbsp. sunflower or olive oil  
- 1 1/2 c. barley (hulless or pearled)  
- 1/4 c. minced shallots  
- 1 small bunch green onions, trimmed and chopped  
- 1/4 c. white wine  
- 4 to 5 c. vegetable or chicken stock  
- 3/4 to 1 lb. spinach, rinsed, dried, and sliced into 1/4-in. strips  
- 1/4 c. chopped fresh parsley  
- Generous pinch of grated nutmeg  
- 1/4 c. shredded aged Parmesan cheese  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste  
- Pinch of red pepper flakes  

**Directions:**

1. Heat the oil in a large deep heavy saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the barley, shallots, and green onions, tossing to coat with the oil. Cook until the shallots are tender, about 3 minutes.

2. Stir in the wine, then add the stock 1/2 cup at a time, allowing the barley to absorb the liquid as you stir. Cook until the barley is tender, about 30 minutes for the pearled barley and 40 to 45 minutes for the hulled barley.

3. Toss in the spinach, parsley, and nutmeg, and stir. Then, fold in the cheese. Season to taste with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.

**Notes:**  
You can prepare the risotto a day in advance. Reheat and add the spinach and cheese just before serving.

**Henri: A Northeast Tropical Storm**

NEW YORK — Henri, downgraded to a tropical storm on Sunday, churned inland across the Northeast. Here’s a breakdown of this unusual weather event:

**Henri's Status and Impact**

Henri, downgraded from hurricane status early Sunday, made landfall in Rhode Island at midday. By Sunday evening, it weakened further while moving over western Massachusetts and Connecticut.  While wind speeds decreased to 40 mph (64 kph), the primary threat remains heavy rainfall, leading to potential storm surges and inland flooding, historically more dangerous than high winds.

Henri veered west after landfall, impacting Connecticut and New York's Hudson River Valley with heavy rain and potential flooding. While the storm surge wasn't as significant as Superstorm Sandy in 2012, the storm's slow movement concentrates rainfall, increasing flood risks.  The storm is forecast to move east early Monday, affecting Vermont and New Hampshire before exiting into the Gulf of Maine.

**Hurricanes vs. Tropical Storms**

The distinction lies in sustained wind speeds. Hurricanes have sustained winds of 74 mph or higher, while tropical storms have sustained winds up to 73 mph.

**Historical Context: Henri, Bob, and Gloria**

Henri’s near-hurricane landfall would have been New England's first in 30 years.  Hurricane Bob in August 1991 caused 17 deaths and $1.5 billion in damage.  Connecticut residents may recall Hurricane Gloria in September 1985, which hit Long Island and Connecticut, resulting in eight deaths and nearly $1 billion in damage.

**Storm Naming Conventions**

The World Meteorological Association assigns human names to Atlantic storms, cycling through a list of 21 names each season.

**Formation and Climate Change**

Two factors contribute to northward-tracking storms: a tropical system and steering currents. While rare, Henri's path isn't directly attributed to climate change, although global warming is known to intensify hurricanes, making them stronger and wetter.

**Preparedness and Comparisons**

Residents are advised to take standard precautions: secure boats, fuel vehicles, stock supplies, and prepare for potential power outages, which could last a week or more. While Henri is unlikely to replicate Superstorm Sandy’s impact on New York City and the Jersey Shore, the Hudson River Valley faces significant flood risk.  Unlike Sandy, Henri provided less preparation time.

**Comparisons to Other Storms**

Henri is unrelated to 1991's "Perfect Storm" (also known as the Halloween Storm), a nor'easter that later developed a hurricane at its center.  This unnamed hurricane would have been called "Henri" due to the six-year recycling of Atlantic hurricane names (excluding retired names like Katrina and Bob).  The 2000 film "The Perfect Storm" depicts this event, not Hurricane Bob. While Hurricane Irene in 2011 impacted Vermont, it had weakened to a tropical storm by then.

**Current Situation and Governor's Status**

Despite some schools returning, tourists remain on the Atlantic coast.  Outgoing Governor Cuomo, whose term ends Monday at 11:59 p.m. EDT, is currently managing the state's response to Henri.

The story begins in the early 1940s at the Foynes Airbase Flying Boat Terminal Building in Limerick, Ireland. Chef Joseph Sheridan created the drink for stranded passengers, combining good Irish whiskey with hot coffee. When a passenger asked if he had used Brazilian coffee, Sheridan famously quipped, "No, that was Irish Coffee!"

The drink's journey to America came through Stanton Delaplane, a San Francisco Chronicle travel writer, who discovered it at Shannon Airport. "I've never been in debt like this," said Dale, a fourth-generation dairy farmer who took over the family farm in 1990. He and his wife, Karen, sat at their kitchen table, surrounded by a mound of paperwork—some detailing milk prices, others highlighting their income struggles.

After unsuccessful appeals to various banks, Dale considered selling part of the farm to make ends meet. However, Karen had a different plan, one she hadn't shared with her husband.

"He's too proud, but I thought if people knew, maybe they would help," she told USA Today Network-Wisconsin.

Karen took to GoFundMe, a crowdfunding platform, to write a heartfelt plea to save the family farm. Her adult children and their friends shared the campaign on Facebook, and donations began to trickle in. As word spread on social media, Karen received calls from local farmers offering help, including one who had extra hay.

The community, including friends, family, and strangers, rallied to prevent the demise of another family farm. Donations poured in from people in other states as well.

Since 1873, the Cihlar family has farmed the 110-acre property, sustaining the family for generations. To handle the historical fluctuations in milk prices, Dale had embraced the budgeting practices of his forebears, saving diligently to cover large expenses and ride out price swings.

Frugality was so ingrained in Dale's psyche that he didn't marry Karen until he made his last payment on the family farm. Although milk prices had been low before, they had never been this low for three consecutive years.

Savings among dairy farmers were depleting across the state. Wisconsin lost 500 dairy farms in 2017, and more than 150 had quit milking cows so far this year. The number of milk herds dropped by 20% from five years ago, according to the state Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection.

The Cihlar farm weathered these highs and lows until a perfect storm of issues hit. The historically low milk checks worsened after several prized cows died, and the $1,600 monthly manure storage system payment drained the farm’s savings.

Dale and Karen managed to squeak by on Karen’s salary from the Door County Medical Center, but their savings were exhausted. For over 100 years, the 110-acre farm and 40 cows had supported the Cihlar family.

"I couldn't be the last one. I've always thought this farm would last and be part of my family far into the future," Dale said.

In less than a month, the GoFundMe page Karen created raised enough money to buy one cow. After a month, they'd raised nearly $8,000 of the $35,000 goal.

"I started to cry. I couldn't believe that people were actually helping us," Karen said.

When Karen showed Dale the GoFundMe site and the donations, he was dumbfounded.

"There are so many causes needing help, and I thought no one would ever want to help a farmer," Dale said, shaking his head. "I was wrong; this is beyond words."

The cost of a dairy cow ranges from $1,000 to $1,600, with significant additional expenses for feed and veterinary care.

While the financial support was crucial, the campaign had a broader impact by highlighting the plight of dairy farmers and showing that people can help. Offers of free feed poured in, and farmers leaving the business sold some stock to the Cihlars at reduced rates to ensure the farm's success.

Dale's extended family also pitched in to keep the farm within the family.

"I'm the only cousin still in farming, and this farm means a lot to them too," he said.

Besides the donations, Dale took a part-time truck-driving job to help make ends meet. Despite knowing firsthand the challenges of dairy farming, both Dale's stepson and son-in-law are determined to keep the farm in the family. They plan to take over when Dale retires, assisting with farm chores while maintaining their day jobs.

"They help out every morning and night and know it's not easy," Dale said.

Ethan Lautenbach, Karen's son from her first marriage, shares Dale's passion for farming.

"It's a challenge every day," Ethan said, adding that he enjoys the lifestyle.

Son-in-law Steven Baxter grew up on a small goat farm in Texas and is president of the Door County Farm Bureau. Like Dale, Steven is captivated by the animals and sees them as integral to the business.

"If it wasn't for their milk, we wouldn't have a dairy," Steven said. "When a calf is born, it's a miracle, and we do everything to ensure it grows up healthy because, in the long run, that cow is what takes care of us."

ROME (Reuters) -  Italy is grappling with a severe coronavirus crisis and a deep economic recession.  On Wednesday, President Sergio Mattarella moved swiftly to address the situation, asking former European Central Bank chief Mario Draghi to form a new government.  Mattarella’s action followed the collapse of outgoing Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte’s coalition government on Tuesday evening.  The president stressed the urgency of the situation, warning that Italy risked missing out on over 200 billion euros ($243 billion) in European Union recovery funds if a new government wasn't formed immediately.

Draghi, renowned for his role in saving the euro zone from collapse in 2012, accepted the mandate.  Expressing confidence in securing parliamentary backing, he acknowledged the challenges ahead: “This is a difficult time. Beating the pandemic, completing the vaccination campaign, offering answers to the everyday problems of the people and relaunching the country are the challenges we face.”  He emphasized the opportunity presented by the EU funds: “We have extraordinary European Union resources at our disposal, we have the opportunity to do so much for our country.”

Investors reacted positively to Draghi's appointment, with Italian borrowing costs poised for their largest single-day drop since June and the Milan bourse blue chip index rising 2.5%.  However, securing the necessary political support is far from guaranteed. The 5-Star Movement, the largest party in parliament, immediately declared its opposition, potentially complicating Draghi's efforts to form a stable government.

Draghi, nicknamed “Super Mario” for his decisive actions at the ECB, where he famously pledged to do “whatever it takes” to save the euro, had largely been out of the public eye since leaving the ECB in October 2019.  His return to the political stage comes as Italy faces a confluence of crises.  As the first European country hit by the coronavirus, Italy has suffered over 89,000 deaths, the sixth-highest toll globally.  Lockdowns implemented to control the virus have ravaged the economy, resulting in an 8.8% GDP contraction in 2020, the steepest decline since World War Two.

*MCLEAN, Va., Feb. 23, 2021* /PRNewswire/ -- Aireon LLC and Avinor Air Navigation Services have announced an agreement to implement space-based Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) technology for monitoring helicopter operations in the Bodo Oceanic Flight Information Region (FIR) and surrounding airspace. The monitored area encompasses the Norwegian Basin and Barents Sea, with surveillance focusing on helicopter movements from ground level through flight level 100. Avinor, a state-owned company under the Norwegian Ministry of Transport and Communications, manages 44 state-owned airports and facilitates travel for approximately 50 million passengers annually.

The implementation of space-based ADS-B technology will provide Avinor with real-time visibility throughout the region, significantly enhancing safety and search and rescue capabilities. This marks the first application of space-based ADS-B specifically designed for helicopter surveillance. The region's helicopter fleet is equipped with ADS-B antennas, enabling the Aireon system to track low-altitude traffic. The surveillance data will be transmitted in real-time to Avinor's facilities and integrated into their air traffic automation platform.

Don Thoma, CEO of Aireon, noted, "Since the Aireon system's deployment in 2019, we've observed exceptional visibility of helicopter movements during pre-operational testing. Avinor's innovative application of our data to enhance safety and rescue operations sets a new standard. This implementation demonstrates that space-based ADS-B is the premier solution for low-altitude monitoring."

Anders Kirsebom, CEO of Avinor Air Navigation Services, added, "Space-based ADS-B technology will be crucial to our Arctic High North surveillance capabilities. We look forward to collaborating with Aireon and anticipate this becoming an essential tool for our air traffic controllers at the Polaris Area Control Centre in Bodø, Norway."

Future plans include potentially expanding the vertical surveillance limit to monitor commercial aircraft at higher altitudes.

## About Aireon LLC
Aireon operates the world's first space-based air traffic surveillance system for ADS-B equipped aircraft. By extending formerly ground-based technologies globally, Aireon enhances aviation efficiency, safety, and environmental sustainability while providing cost benefits to stakeholders. Aireon partners with leading ANSPs worldwide, including NAV CANADA, Enav, NATS, the Irish Aviation Authority (IAA), and Naviair, alongside Iridium Communications. Avinor Air Navigation Services leads Norway's air navigation services and pioneers digital Remote Towers systems and UTM. Avinor ANS was among Europe's first ANSPs to implement Free Route Airspace and leads in curved approaches and direct climb and descent procedures. The organization serves approximately 50 airports and provides en-route services through three control centers.

One of the things you can do is go down there. Go down to the convention center tomorrow between 11 and 1 and show your support for law enforcement.”

What did Jones expect? Emotions were already running high over the shooting death of Deputy Mark Stasyuk, a 27-year-old killed on Monday during a routine call in Rancho Cordova.

Choosing such a solemn moment to make a political statement under the guise of a call to action was ill-timed. And people responded. Groups, mainly older individuals, some carrying American flags and a couple wearing red "Make America Great Again" hats similar to those worn by President Donald Trump, gathered to support law enforcement and confront BLM.

The BLM group included clergy, a mix of white and African American individuals, and a diverse array of supporters. The pro-law enforcement side was primarily composed of older white individuals, along with some younger participants. I didn’t stay for the entire event, but I witnessed the tensest moments firsthand.

This clash of ideologies was on the verge of exploding.

As Leong worked to maintain peace, Jones' office issued a clarification on his earlier comments: “Sheriff Jones never called for a counterprotest—which would encourage responding persons to protest or address the planned protest directly—but rather gave the community an outlet for their grief and support where over a hundred Sheriff’s Department personnel and law enforcement from around the state will be gathered to learn better ways to police their communities.”

Really?

Re-read what Jones said on Monday and determine his true intent. It seemed like he was trying to correct one misstep by making another.

Claudio Ranieri has strongly criticized Aboubakar Kamara for displaying disrespect towards his Fulham teammates, supporters, and the club by disregarding instructions and taking a crucial penalty, which he missed, potentially jeopardizing their victory against Huddersfield.

Fulham ultimately secured three vital points with a 1-0 win, thanks to Aleksandar Mitrovic’s stoppage-time goal. Earlier in the match, Kamara ignored Mitrovic, the club’s designated penalty taker, opting to take the penalty himself, which was subsequently saved by Huddersfield's Jonas Lossl at 0-0.

Kamara had previously scored from the penalty spot in a 4-1 defeat against Manchester United earlier this month. However, the normally composed 67-year-old Ranieri was visibly upset that Kamara “thought only of himself” and suggested he might consider dropping him from the team for his actions, which Ranieri claimed he had never encountered before.

Ranieri expressed his frustration, stating, “It is not possible to explain what happened after we got the penalty, or maybe I should say it is easy when a man thinks only of himself. It is not right. He didn’t respect me, the club, his teammates, the crowd. He took the ball and just said, ‘I want to shoot.’ He didn’t listen to reason.”

Ranieri continued, “I have spoken a little to him. I think he didn’t understand what I said. Mitrovic was the designated taker, but Kamara scored our last penalty and took it on himself, ‘I am the man.’ He did not apologize, he just told me ‘I wanted to shoot.’ I said to him, ‘If the whole team just said I want to shoot, what would happen?’ It is impossible to speak to this man.”

Ranieri further lamented, “He did not understand the reason; for him, everything is fine, we won the match. It is unbelievable; the first time in my life I have seen that. I understand why the fans might boo him, but of course, it is better if the fans and us are altogether. You must respect the nominated taker.”

Considering Kamara’s future in the team, Ranieri said, “I hope he can understand; it is clearly difficult. I don’t know if that is it, if it is finished or if it will continue. Maybe I will take him away from the squad. But I will do what is best for the squad. If it is good for them, he plays. If I think it isn’t, he comes out. We’ll play the Arsenal match on Tuesday, then I decide. The other players are calm because we won – but not me. It is not important whether we won or lost, it is important what you did and why.”

Mitrovic’s last-minute goal left Huddersfield at the bottom of the Premier League, having lost all seven of their league fixtures this month. Their manager, David Wagner, reflected on their current situation, saying, “Obviously it’s a low point. Not only because we’ve lost seven in a row but how we lost it. It’s a heavy loss we’ve conceded at Fulham. We will need for sure a little bit longer than only 30 minutes afterwards to deal with it. December wasn’t our month, obviously. But for me, it’s not possible to think so quickly after the game about the transfer window or the next game. I have to reflect. It’s very difficult.”

Press Association

# The Inspiring Story of Uche Ikoro: Ability in Disability

## Introduction
Uche Ikoro, a 23-year-old father of two from Abiriba in Abia state, works as a commercial cab driver with Eastern Mass Transit. Despite being born with no legs and partially deformed arms, he operates routes between Enugu, Ebonyi, Anambra, and beyond. His story exemplifies triumph over physical challenges and society's expectations.

## Professional Journey
Our correspondent, who encountered Ikoro at the Eastern Mass Transit Terminal in Holy Ghost Enugu on December 27, 2020, witnessed his remarkable ability to manipulate the vehicle's controls. His exceptional driving skills, demonstrated over six years in the profession, have earned him recognition as one of the most respected commercial drivers in the southeast region.

Before becoming a driver, Ikoro worked as a building engineer and solar light installer. He began his driving career in 2015, initially operating on the Lagos route before focusing on the southeast region for better returns. The transition to commercial driving was made possible through the generosity of Very Reverend Father Professor Johnbosco Akam, who provided him with his first cab.

## Personal Philosophy
"In this life, if you believe in God, God will believe in you," Ikoro states. He firmly believes that his physical condition should not condemn him to a life of begging or poverty. Speaking impeccable English and holding a Senior School Certificate with excellent grades, Ikoro chose not to pursue further education to focus on supporting his family.

## Views on Begging and Disability
Ikoro strongly opposes begging as a means of survival for persons with disabilities. He emphasizes that "begging can not empower anyone because more efforts were required to break even." He considers it dehumanizing and believes it reduces individuals to social misfits.

Rodney Rice entered his home state of West Virginia on a Sunday afternoon. The singer-songwriter from Littleton had just left Nashville after spending four days in a recording studio, marking his first proper visit to the country music hub. He was en route to visit family and install a kayak rack on his vehicle.

Despite the unconventional timing for travel, Rodney had been isolated for months and was eager to record new songs. Despite the challenges of the year, he remained productive. 

"I’m adhering to safety measures, wearing a mask, and carrying hand sanitizer," Rice said. "Everyone in the studio was diligent about it too, we were all masked up. I’m just trying to make my way across the country as safely as possible."

Rodney was thrilled that his upcoming second album, SAME SHIrT, DIFFERENT DAY, set to release on streaming platforms on October 23, was gaining attention. The album, labeled as “Bubblin’ Up” on the Americana Music Association’s chart, features twelve tracks of gritty, twangy country-rock with an array of guest musicians. The songs touch on themes like critiquing the current presidential administration and the struggles of a corporate job.

This album follows his 2014 debut, Empty Pockets and a Troubled Mind. Rodney felt more at ease in the studio this time around and found inspiration in the tumultuous state of the world.

"I prefer the second one," he remarked. "The songs feel more current and relevant. The first album included some of the earliest songs I had ever written, spanning from high school to the recording session. It covered a broader time frame."

The opening track of SAME SHIrT, DIFFERENT DAY, titled “Ain’t Got a Dollar,” delves into the presidency of Trump and the notion that politics often revolves around money. Rodney expressed his embarrassment over having a reality TV star as the country's leader, incorporating military references influenced by his family and friends' military service.

Rodney's upbringing in West Virginia, with its blend of city life and rural surroundings where darkness descends early in the “hollers,” has shaped his musical style. He believes Appalachia shares common daily life aspects across regions like West Virginia, Tennessee, and Kentucky, emphasizing the value of diverse experiences.

After returning to West Virginia to attend the University of West Virginia for a degree in geology, Rodney spent years in the oil industry before transitioning to focus on his music full-time. His time in Texas on oil rigs influenced his music, with songs like “Middle Managed Blues” drawing from his corporate job experiences.

Moving to Colorado after meeting a woman from Boulder, Rodney immersed himself in music during his Texas days, watching performances by outlaw country legend Billy Joe Shaver, who played a significant role in Rodney's musical journey.

Rodney's early exposure to music, raiding his sister’s collection of Uncle Tupelo, Waylon Jennings, and Shaver tapes and CDs, left a lasting impression. Attending a concert by John Prine at a young age further fueled his passion for music.

SAME SHIrT, DIFFERENT DAY will be available on October 23. For more information on how to access the album, visit Rodney Rice's website.

West Coast premiership big man Nathan Vardy seems to have secured the spot as Nic Naitanui's ruck partner for round one of the AFL season. Naitanui made a successful return to the field in the pre-season match against Fremantle, recording 22 hit-outs from five possessions before coming off in the third quarter. This game was crucial for Naitanui, as it was his only match of the pre-season following a hamstring injury over the summer.

Given the return to full-length matches this year, West Coast is looking to provide more support for Naitanui in the ruck. Vardy, who didn't play in the AFL last year due to a serious leg condition, appears to be the likely choice to support Naitanui. With Bailey Williams nursing an ankle injury, Vardy's strong performance in the pre-season games puts him in a good position for a round-one call-up against Gold Coast.

In terms of Oscar Allen, his role in the team for the upcoming season remains uncertain. Allen was the primary ruck support for Naitanui last year, but the Eagles are considering using a recognized ruckman like Vardy or Williams in that role in 2021. Coach Adam Simpson mentioned that Allen has been versatile during the pre-season, alternating between roles in attack and defense. With the potential return of Josh Kennedy for round one, Allen may see more playing time in defense.

The Eagles are dealing with several injury concerns as they approach the start of the season. Star midfielder Tim Kelly missed both pre-season games due to a thumb injury but is expected to be fit for round one. Captain Luke Shuey sustained an ankle injury in the match against Fremantle but is likely to be available for the season opener. On the other hand, recruit Zac Langdon suffered a serious concussion and is unlikely to be selected for round one.

Furthermore, onballer Elliot Yeo will be sidelined at the beginning of the season due to ongoing issues with osteitis pubis. Although there are options to consider, such as defender Harry Edwards, the Eagles are leaning towards a more traditional ruck setup for round one. With uncertainties surrounding the roles of players like Allen and Vardy, West Coast will continue to assess their options leading up to the start of the AFL season.

The Arizona Cardinals recently reduced their roster to 52 players, leaving an open spot due to two players on the COVID list and one player returning imminently. The team will likely make further adjustments through waiver claims and free agents, but we now have a clear view of the initial 53-man roster.

Here is a breakdown of the positions and players on the roster:

Quarterbacks:
The top two quarterback spots were secure, with the decision revolving around whether Streveler would make the final 53. In today's NFL climate, having three capable quarterbacks is vital, especially given ongoing COVID concerns. The team values Streveler and may opt to keep him on the roster to avoid exposing him to waivers.

Running back:
The running back group consists of Chase Edmonds, James Conner, Eno Benjamin, and Jonathan Ward. The challenge ahead will be determining the depth chart and game-day activations among these four players.

Wide receivers:
DeAndre Hopkins, A.J. Green, Christian Kirk, Rondale Moore, Andy Isabella, and Antoine Wesley comprise the wide receiver corps. While the Cardinals were expected to carry six receivers, some surprises emerged in the final selection, notably Wesley making the cut over others like Greg Dortch.

Tight end:
Dan Arnold, Maxx Williams, and Darrell Daniels form the tight end group, with Ross Travis a potential practice squad candidate.

Offensive line:
The offensive line includes D.J. Humphries, Justin Murray, Rodney Hudson, Brian Winters, Kelvin Beachum, Josh Jones, Max Garcia, and Josh Miles. Once Justin Pugh returns from the COVID reserve, the line will be complete with nine linemen.

Defensive line:
J.J. Watt, Rashard Lawrence, Jordan Phillips, Zach Allen, Leki Fotu, Corey Peters, and Michael Dogbe make up the defensive line group. Dogbe's presence on the roster was unexpected due to the numbers game, with the possibility of a seventh lineman being carried.

Outside linebacker:
Chandler Jones, Markus Golden, Devon Kennard, Dennis Gardeck, and Victor Dimukeje are the outside linebackers. Gardeck's return from the PUP list required him to be on the roster, while Dimukeje's inclusion was not surprising given his preseason performance.

Inside linebacker:
Zaven Collins, Isaiah Simmons, Jordan Hicks, Tanner Vallejo, and Zeke Turner complete the inside linebacker group. Turner's special teams prowess adds depth to the position.

Cornerback:
Byron Murphy, Marco Wilson, Tay Gowan, and Luq Barcoo currently fill the cornerback spots, with Robert Alford set to return from the COVID list. Malcolm Butler's sudden retirement has left a gap to be addressed in the secondary.

Safety:
Budda Baker, Jalen Thompson, Deionte Thompson, and Charles Washington make up the safety group. The decision to cut three safeties, including established players like Chris Banjo and Shawn Williams, was unexpected but highlights the depth in this position.

Specialists:
The specialists—Matt Prater, Andy Lee, and Aaron Brewer—remain unchanged, with potential practice squad additions like punter Ryan Winslow for backup purposes.

The Cardinals' roster decisions reflect a mix of expected choices and surprising outcomes, setting the stage for further adjustments as the season progresses.

Tanzanian President John Magufuli has confidently declared that his country has successfully eradicated coronavirus, attributing this achievement to the power of prayer, the efforts of local health officials, and frontline healthcare workers. He emphasized the importance of continued vigilance and precautionary measures despite the positive outlook.

Magufuli's remarks were made during a speech delivered at a church in Dodoma, the capital city of Tanzania, where he commended churchgoers for not wearing masks as a symbol of the country's victory over the virus and the diminishing fear among the population.

While the President claimed that there were only four Covid-19 patients left in hospitals in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania has not reported any new data on coronavirus cases since April 29. The last available figures from the World Health Organization indicated 509 reported cases and 21 deaths in the country.

Concerns have been raised by regional WHO officials regarding Tanzania's approach to social distancing and the decision to keep places of worship open despite the risks associated with large gatherings. The US Embassy in Tanzania issued a health alert in May, warning of the high risk of contracting Covid-19 due to overwhelmed hospitals in Dar es Salaam.

President Magufuli initially downplayed the seriousness of the virus in Tanzania, urging citizens to rely on prayer to combat the disease and dismissing the reported increase in positive cases as a result of faulty test kits. Despite this, the country has started to ease coronavirus restrictions, with universities, high schools, and international travel resuming while primary and secondary schools remain closed.

Located in the Leesville area of Lake Murray, Hollow Creek Distillery is a charming retreat where visitors can wander off the beaten path, enjoy warm Southern hospitality, and escape the hustle and bustle of everyday life.

Nestled in the trees, you'll find a quaint little red barn with white rocking chairs on the front porch. From there, you can sit back, relax, and gaze out at the wide expanse of the lake across Highway 378. Typically, on a springtime Saturday, guests could wander inside, learn about the art of moonshine-making, and savor some of Craig and Meredith Amick's handcrafted spirits.

However, this spring is far from ordinary at Hollow Creek. Instead of welcoming guests and offering a taste of their fine Southern moonshine, Hollow Creek Distillery has pivoted to a life-saving mission.

Recently, the Amicks received a call from the State of South Carolina, asking if they would be willing to use their moonshine still to produce hand sanitizer. Without hesitation, they agreed to assist their fellow South Carolinians on the front lines of the battle against the coronavirus.

"At first, we thought it was a joke, but it turned out to be very real," Meredith Amick remarked, standing next to Hollow Creek's substantial still. "So, we had to make some adjustments here."

For two weeks straight, the Amicks worked tirelessly, putting in 14-hour days operating the moonshine still to meet the State's urgent request. Last week, they delivered 1,375 gallon jugs of their clear, potent germ-killing solution to the state's Department of Transportation, which is overseeing the distribution to those in critical need.

"It was a privilege to be called upon by the State government to contribute to this cause," Mrs. Amick stated. "This is our home, and we are grateful to be able to support the community and state that have played a significant role in our lives and education.

Louise Kenny, a professor of obstetrics and a consultant obstetrician and gynaecologist, has witnessed the adverse impact of the Eighth Amendment on pregnant women with cancer. She emphasized that the Eighth Amendment casts a shadow over the care of women with complex medical needs in Ireland. In response to a previous opinion article by Prof Eamon McGuinness, Prof Kenny refuted claims that the Eighth Amendment does not endanger pregnant women's lives.

Prof Kenny cited the case of Michelle Harte, a woman who had to travel to Britain for an abortion while terminally ill with cancer. Despite being advised to terminate her pregnancy by doctors at Cork University Hospital, the hospital's ethics committee concluded that there was no immediate risk to Ms Harte's life and advised against termination.

Prof Kenny highlighted the challenges faced by pregnant women with cancer in accessing advanced cancer treatments that are often available only through clinical trials. She stressed the importance of having clear guidelines and legal interpretations to ensure timely and appropriate care for such patients.

Ms Harte's tragic case underscored the limitations imposed by the Eighth Amendment on women's healthcare choices. Despite the State providing substantial compensation to Ms Harte, she passed away in 2011. Prof Kenny urged for an open and respectful debate on the issue to ensure that decisions are made based on facts rather than opinions.

In conclusion, the Eighth Amendment has had real-life implications for pregnant women with cancer in Ireland. Prof Kenny's advocacy for the repeal of this amendment is rooted in her firsthand experiences of the obstacles it creates for women seeking essential medical care. The need for clarity, compassion, and evidence-based decision-making in women's healthcare cannot be overstated.

Hugh Jackman, much like the character he portrays, is nearing the end of his tenure with the superhero realm. Once again, he's poised to don the muttonchops and CGI adamantium claws for his role in "Logan." However, Jackman insists that this will be his final performance as Wolverine, promising to retire the cigar and claws for good. We've heard similar claims before, as it seems that every Wolverine appearance is touted as his last. But this time, Jackman assures us, he truly means it—unless circumstances change.

In a conversation with ScreenRant about "Logan," Jackman suggested there might still be one adventure left for him, albeit contingent on a nearly impossible collaboration between 20th Century Fox and Marvel Studios. He expressed, "If [an Avengers movie] was on the table when I made my decision, it certainly would have made me pause. That’s for sure. Because I always love the idea of him within that dynamic, with the Hulk obviously. […] At the moment, honestly, if I really did have [the Avengers] there, I probably wouldn’t have said this is the last [movie]."

Considering the logistical challenges, it's clear that coordinating rival movie studio executives is akin to corralling a bag full of wet cats—it's chaotic and usually unproductive. However, the successful collaboration between Sony Pictures and Marvel for Spider-Man sets a precedent. If they could reach a custody arrangement, there's no reason Fox can't take similar steps. Even if Fox is hesitant to concede any control to Marvel, would they really leave potential profits on the table? With the Infinity Stones storyline, it’s conceivable that Wolverine could be pulled into the Avengers universe for a movie or two.

# Internet Governance Conference Shifts Focus as US Signals Change

A global conference on Internet governance in Brazil is expected to be less contentious than initially anticipated, following the United States' willingness to relax its control over key Internet functions.

The US has agreed to relinquish oversight of the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) - a California-based nonprofit responsible for managing domain names - responding to demands from Brazil and other nations following revelations of widespread electronic surveillance.

"The focus has shifted from a political reaction to the NSA allegations toward more constructive criticism and dialogue about the Internet's future," notes William Beer, a São Paulo-based cybersecurity expert.

The Net Mundial conference, a two-day event in São Paulo opening Wednesday under Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff, will address several crucial topics:

- Cybersecurity
- Privacy protection
- Freedom of expression
- Future oversight of the decentralized network

Representatives from diverse nations - including China, Cuba, the United States, and European countries - will participate. However, organizers emphasize that government officials will share equal standing with:

- Internet companies
- Academic institutions
- Technical experts
- Internet user advocacy groups

"All stakeholders deserve equal participation in this multi-stakeholder process," explains Virgilio Almeida, Brazil's IT policy secretary and conference chair.

While the conference isn't expected to produce binding decisions, Almeida suggests it will initiate an important dialogue that will "sow the seeds" for future Internet governance reforms.

## Background and Context

The conference emerges from controversy surrounding NSA surveillance programs, which targeted multiple world leaders, including:

- Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff
- German Chancellor Angela Merkel

These revelations, disclosed by former NSA analyst Edward Snowden, prompted international calls to reduce US control over the Internet - a network originally created 50 years ago to connect American universities with the defense industry.

## ICANN Transition

In a surprising move last month, the US government announced plans to transfer ICANN oversight to an international body by September 2015. This transition comes with one crucial condition: the new organization cannot be under any government's control.

The debate over ICANN's future management likely represents a new point of contention, particularly with nations advocating for multilateral control through organizations like the United Nations.

China, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan have jointly proposed developing a UN-based Internet code of conduct. However, this proposal - originating from countries known for Internet censorship - is unlikely to gain widespread support at the conference.

"Most participants here favor a multi-stakeholder model for the Internet," Almeida told Reuters. "China prefers a UN treaty approach, but the UN only represents governments."

A ManpowerGroup survey of 5,110 employers found that only 16 percent plan to increase their workforce in the quarter ending in September. "Diversity, automated recruitment, virtual reality, and remote working options are major trends expected to drive recruitment in India in 2018," AG Rao, Group Managing Director of ManpowerGroup India, said in a statement Tuesday. The service sector and wholesale and retail trade anticipate the strongest hiring outlook, with 20 percent of respondents in these sectors indicating plans to hire in the September quarter.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is relying on robust economic growth to generate jobs before the 2019 general elections.  GDP growth has accelerated for four consecutive quarters, reaching 7.7 percent in the quarter ending in March.

Modi's 2014 campaign promised the creation of 10 million jobs.  Four years later, the actual number of jobs created remains unclear.  Government data indicates that over 12 million Indians enter the workforce annually.

While hiring isn't significantly increasing, data suggests that large-scale job losses are also absent. According to data compiled by the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE), the unemployment rate fell to 5.29 percent in May from 5.64 percent the previous month, the lowest since January.  Official government unemployment data for 2018 is not yet available.

"A significant portion of the recent growth acceleration stems from increased public administration spending," said Mahesh Vyas, CEO of CMIE.  "This is not sustainable, and therefore, the nature of the current growth imposes inherent limitations."

# Antarctica's Hidden Heat: New Evidence Supports Mantle Plume Theory

Three decades ago, a University of Colorado Denver scientist proposed an intriguing hypothesis: a mantle plume beneath Marie Byrd Land could explain both the region's volcanic activity and its distinctive topographic dome. Recent seismic imaging has now validated this theory, though it initially met with skepticism. "I thought it was crazy," admitted Hélène Seroussi of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). "The concept of such intense heat coexisting with an ice sheet seemed implausible."

A groundbreaking NASA study has now provided compelling evidence for this geothermal heat source deep beneath Antarctica. While this mantle plume doesn't pose a new or escalating threat to the West Antarctic ice sheet, it offers crucial insights into two phenomena: the sheet's rapid collapse during previous periods of climate change and its current instability.

The ice sheet's stability depends heavily on its basal lubrication—the water underneath that facilitates glacial movement. Understanding these subglacial water sources and their future behavior is crucial for predicting future ice loss to the ocean.

Beneath Antarctica's bedrock lies an intricate network of rivers and lakes, including one that rivals Lake Erie in size. These water bodies exhibit dynamic behavior, with rapid filling and draining cycles that can cause the overhead ice surface—thousands of feet thick—to fluctuate by up to 20 feet (6 meters). These movements enable scientists to calculate the volume and distribution of subglacial water.

Given the scarcity of direct measurements beneath the ice, Seroussi and colleague Erik Ivins of JPL turned to numerical modeling. They employed the Ice Sheet System Model (ISSM), a sophisticated numerical representation of ice sheet physics developed by JPL and UC Irvine researchers. Seroussi enhanced the model to account for various heat sources and transport mechanisms, including:

- Natural heating processes
- Heat transport from phase changes
- Frictional effects
- Other thermal phenomena

To validate their model, the researchers utilized surface altitude data from NASA's IceSat satellite and Operation IceBridge flights. "These observations provided crucial constraints on possible melt rates—precisely what we aimed to predict," explained Ivins. The team ran numerous simulations testing various plume parameters, given the uncertainty about the mantle plume's exact location and dimensions.

Their findings revealed that the mantle plume's energy flux cannot exceed 150 milliwatts per square meter. For context:
- Typical U.S. regions without volcanic activity: 40-60 milliwatts
- Yellowstone National Park (average): 200 milliwatts
- Individual geothermal features: Significantly higher

The simulations identified one exceptional area inland from the Ross Sea, characterized by intense water flows, requiring 150-180 milliwatts per square meter to match observations. Seismic data suggests this heat reaches the ice through a crustal rift, similar to Africa's Great Rift Valley.

Mantle plumes are theorized to be narrow streams of hot rock that rise through Earth's mantle, spreading mushroom-like beneath the crust. This concept, proposed in the 1970s, explains geothermal activity far from tectonic plate boundaries, such as in Hawaii and Yellowstone.

French newspaper Les Echos suggested a scenario where ST-Ericsson could be sold piecemeal, with technologies like connectivity, power management, and software architecture attracting different buyers.  Remaining parts of the business might be reabsorbed by the parent companies. While no decision has been announced, one is expected by the end of the year.

In the second quarter, it reported an operating loss of $235 million, attributed to the collapsing demand for feature phones from clients like Nokia and Sony Ericsson, and the challenging transition to supplying chips for the smartphone market.  The company’s full-year 2011 loss totaled $841 million on sales of $1.65 billion, and it has accumulated losses of around $2 billion over its three years of operation.

While Ericsson and STMicroelectronics have publicly stated their support for ST-Ericsson's ongoing cost-cutting initiatives aimed at lowering the break-even point, analysts are skeptical about the prospects of a sale.  "The possibilities for Ericsson are limited except to hold on to its share and try and do the turnaround themselves," said Mirko Maier, analyst at LBBW. Finding a buyer for the entire business, or even substantial parts of it, appears challenging given its financial performance.

This two-acre holding pen, located behind the Caddo Correctional Center, is designed to accommodate horses, cows, goats, domestic pigs, and donkeys that frequently escape from pastures and other enclosures within the parish.

The Sheriff’s Office Stock Patrol retrieves loose livestock on a weekly—and sometimes daily—basis. Some animals remain for just a few hours until their owners are found, while others may stay for several weeks. If the owners cannot be identified, the animals are advertised for ten days before being auctioned off.

This often means the animal will be housed by the Caddo Sheriff’s Office for an extended period,” explained Sheriff Steve Prator.

The new facility features three covered holding areas, a gated unloading zone, and a barn equipped with two stalls. It was constructed by the Sheriff's Office's Building and Grounds and Livestock Patrol teams.

The total cost of building the holding pen was approximately $17,000, which includes donations and in-kind services.

Tech giants have transformed our daily lives, yet governments worldwide are increasingly concerned about their growing influence. Known collectively as GAFAM—Google, Apple, Facebook, Amazon, and Microsoft—these companies face accusations of tax evasion, unfair competition, media content theft, and the spread of fake news.

As the European Union prepares to unveil measures to regulate these companies on December 15, here is a global overview of ongoing regulatory efforts:

**Taxation**

The 27-member EU has yet to reach a consensus on taxing digital giants, but individual member states are taking action. France and Italy have implemented a three percent tax on their turnover, Austria has imposed a five percent tax on advertising revenues, and Spain has introduced a three percent charge on specific activities. Outside the EU, the United Kingdom has instituted a two percent tax on certain digital services. Beyond Europe, India imposed a tax on online advertising in 2016, while Australia applied a 10 percent VAT on digital services such as streaming, downloading games and apps, e-books, and data storage. These measures have angered the United States, home to these tech giants, which has threatened reciprocal tariffs. Meanwhile, negotiations for a global tax on multinationals, led by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, stalled in October.

**Competition**

Digital giants are frequently criticized for their market dominance and sidelining of competitors. Between 2017 and 2019, the EU fined Google 8.25 billion euros ($10 billion) for market dominance via its Android system, a decision Google is contesting in court. In 2013, the EU fined Microsoft 561 million euros for forcing users of Windows 7 to use its Internet Explorer search engine. Amazon and Apple are also under investigation for potential breaches of EU competition laws. In the U.S., federal and state antitrust authorities filed lawsuits against Facebook on December 9, challenging its acquisitions of Instagram and WhatsApp. Additionally, in October, the Justice Department and 11 states initiated proceedings against Google for allegedly strengthening its monopoly on online searches and advertising illegally.

**Personal Data**

Tech giants frequently face criticism over their collection and use of personal data.

TAIPEI (Reuters) - Taiwan's exports reached an unprecedented high in December, reinforcing confidence that robust global technology demand will sustain the island's economic growth momentum through 2018.

According to the finance ministry's statistics department, December exports rose 14.8% year-over-year, surpassing the Reuters poll forecast of 9.45% and November's 14.0% growth. This marked the 15th consecutive month of export growth and set a new volume record for a single month.

The ministry attributed this success to several factors: "The strengthening global economic recovery, robust demand for mobile devices and consumer electronics, and rising international raw material prices all contributed to December's record-breaking performance."

- Exports to China increased 16.8%, matching November's growth
- U.S.-bound shipments grew 12.4%, following November's 14.6% expansion
- Strong demand persisted for integrated circuits and machinery
- International crude oil and basic metal prices showed continued strength

## Looking Ahead

The export sector grew 13.2% overall in 2017, positioning Taiwan's economy favorably for 2018, though a strengthening Taiwan dollar and rising global interest rates could impact momentum.

Kevin Wang, an analyst at Taishin investment advisory company, notes: "While we expect January exports to maintain single-digit growth, first-quarter export growth may slightly lag behind fourth-quarter performance." # Nigeria's Economic Downturn: Oil Sector Struggles Amid Global Crisis

Nigeria's oil and gas sector experienced a significant decline in its economic contribution during the second quarter of 2020, driven by plummeting oil prices and diminished global demand. This downturn marked the first economic contraction in over three years, with the nation's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) falling by 6.10%, a stark contrast to the 1.87% growth recorded in the previous quarter.

According to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), the oil sector's performance deteriorated dramatically:

- Q1 2020: 5.06% growth
- Q2 2020: 6.63% year-on-year decline
- Overall decrease: 13.80% compared to Q2 2019

The sector's contribution to total real GDP also diminished:
- Q2 2020: 8.93%
- Q1 2020: 9.50%
- Q2 2019: 8.98%

## Production Challenges

Daily oil production faced significant constraints:
- Q2 2020: 1.81 million barrels per day
- Q1 2020: 2.07 million barrels per day
- Q2 2019: 2.02 million barrels per day

The OPEC+ agreement in April 2020 implemented unprecedented production cuts of 9.7 million barrels per day for May and June, later extended through July. Despite Nigeria's assigned cap of 1.41 million barrels per day, the country exceeded its quota during this period.

## Economic Impact

The Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) attributed the production decline to:
- OPEC+ production cut agreement
- Accumulated unsold crude inventory
- Weakening oil prices (Q2 2020: $33/barrel vs Q1 2020: $51/barrel)

The situation improved marginally as Brent crude prices recovered from April's low of $16 per barrel to $45.91 by Tuesday evening (Nigeria time).

## Broader Economic Context

Budget Office Director-General Ben Akabueze highlighted the severity of the situation:
- Oil revenues declined by nearly 90%
- Oil and gas sector represents:
  - 10% of Nigeria's GDP
  - 50% of government revenues
  - 90% of export earnings

## Power Sector Performance

The electricity sector also experienced significant challenges:
- Q2 2020: 8.64% year-on-year growth (down from 29.75% in Q2 2019)
- Nominal GDP contribution increased to 0.92% (up from 0.82% in Q2 2019)

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) —  After nearly two weeks of massive protests and political turmoil ignited by leaked crude and insulting chat messages between him and his top advisers, Puerto Rico Gov. Ricardo Rosselló announced his resignation late Wednesday, effective Aug. 2.

The 40-year-old son of a former governor, Rosselló becomes the first chief executive to resign in the modern history of Puerto Rico, a U.S. territory of more than 3 million American citizens.  Justice Secretary Wanda Vázquez will assume the post less than halfway through Rosselló’s four-year term, becoming Puerto Rico’s second female governor.

Rosselló’s announcement, delivered on Facebook just before midnight, sparked an eruption of cheers and singing from the thousands gathered outside the governor’s mansion in Old San Juan.  In a video address, a shaken-looking Rosselló listed his accomplishments before confirming his resignation.  “My only priority has been the transformation of our island and the well-being of our people,” he said. Acknowledging the protests, he added, “The demands have been overwhelming and I’ve received them with the highest degree of humility.”

Rosselló’s announcement came after a bizarre, hours-long standoff.  Having pledged to deliver a message to the people of Puerto Rico, the governor remained inexplicably silent for hours as thousands of protesters chanted for his resignation.  An announcement initially expected at 5 p.m. finally arrived less than a half-hour before midnight. “Despite expecting to serve the term that the people democratically elected me to, today I feel that continuing in this position represents a threat to the success we have achieved,” Rosselló said.

Puerto Rico Rep. Gabriel Rodríguez, a member of Rosselló’s pro-statehood party, told The Associated Press that legislators initially agreed to suspend impeachment proceedings and give the governor until 5 p.m. to announce his resignation.

**Columbia Generating Station Achieves Record-Breaking Nuclear Energy Production in 2018**

RICHLAND, Wash., Jan. 08, 2019 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Columbia Generating Station, the third-largest electricity generator in Washington State, achieved a historic milestone in 2018, producing more clean nuclear energy than any other year in its 34-year operating history.  Surpassing the previous record set in 2016, Columbia delivered over 9.7 million megawatt-hours of electricity to the Northwest power grid.  This marks the fifth new generation record in the last seven years.

This consistent increase in output since 2011 stems from ongoing maintenance and upgrades, which have added approximately 60 megawatts to Columbia’s capacity, bringing its current output to 1,207 megawatts (gross). This is enough clean energy to power Seattle and a portion of its metropolitan area.

“It’s about mitigating climate change one clean megawatt at a time, while providing reliable, low-cost electricity 24/7 throughout the Northwest,” said Energy Northwest CEO Brad Sawatzke.  “Our team’s outstanding work in enhancing nuclear performance continues to lower electricity costs for consumers.”

Energy Northwest projects an average cost of power for Columbia of 4.2 cents per kilowatt-hour during its 2018-2019 fuel cycle, a significant decrease from 6.3 cents (adjusted for inflation) during the 2010-2011 cycle.  Columbia refuels every two years, leading to higher costs during refueling years and lower costs during full-run years. Therefore, generation costs are measured in two-year averages, as shown below:

**Columbia Generation Station Cost of Power (2010-2019)**

| Fuel Cycle (fiscal years) | Cost Per Kilowatt-Hour |
|---|---|
| FY10-11 | 6.30¢ |
| FY12-13 | 5.75¢ |
| FY14-15 | 5.10¢ |
| FY16-17 | 4.70¢ |
| FY18-19 (Estimate) | 4.20¢ |

This cost-effectiveness compares favorably to 2018 EIA estimates for new generation resources potentially entering service by 2022: 4.8 cents for advanced combined-cycle natural gas, 4.7 cents for solar (including a 1.3 cent taxpayer subsidy), and 3.7 cents for onshore wind (including a 1.1 cent taxpayer subsidy).

Washington State enjoys the lowest retail electricity costs in the United States, averaging 7.25 cents per kilowatt-hour over the past five years, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Since 2012, Columbia has maintained an average capacity factor of 92 percent, significantly exceeding national averages for other energy sources.

Former deputy FBI director Andrew McCabe is suing the FBI and the Department of Justice (DOJ), alleging they refused to provide him with documents related to his firing. Attorney General Jeff Sessions fired McCabe on March 16, just two days before he was set to retire, on the recommendation of FBI and DOJ officials. McCabe, who joined the FBI in 1996 and was named to the No. 2 position 20 years later, became the bureau's acting leader following the firing in May 2017 of James Comey as director.

The case pits the career law enforcement official against a Justice Department that employed him for more than two decades. It refocuses attention on a firing last March that divided current and former DOJ officials and signals that McCabe, repeatedly targeted for criticism and attacks by President Trump, is determined to clear his name in court. McCabe faces a possible criminal probe into whether he intentionally misled internal investigators. The inspector general's office concluded in a report earlier this year that McCabe had repeatedly deceived investigators and referred the matter for potential criminal prosecution to the U.S. attorney's office in Washington. McCabe has denied the allegations, stating that he tried to correct the record when he thought his answers were being misunderstood during interviews with investigators.

In the lawsuit filed in federal court in Washington, McCabe's lawyers assert that the DOJ has publicly defended the firing yet failed to identify for McCabe the policies and procedures it followed before dismissing him. The department has allegedly withheld the information for fear that the materials could be used against them in additional lawsuits. "We don't create or adjudicate under secret law or procedure," David Snyder, one of McCabe's lawyers, said in an email to The Associated Press. The complaint quotes a May 21 email from one DOJ official stating, "In the absence of actual litigation, (Plaintiff's) demands are not constrained by the normal rules of discovery, which exist, in part, to protect defendants from burdensome or otherwise unreasonable requests."

Among the records being sought are an inspector general manual that outlines the guidelines governing the office and FBI policy guides on handling disciplinary matters. The lawsuit claims that the inspector general's office refused to make the manual available for public review and denied multiple requests to provide it, also denying the lawyers access to a library or reading room where the materials could have been reviewed. The complaint also alleges that the FBI and DOJ failed to disclose a series of requested FBI documents, preventing McCabe and his lawyers from knowing whether appropriate procedures were followed before the firing.

McCabe's lawyers emphasize that they seek the records to vindicate his rights and restore his good name, as they weigh whether to take more legal action over what they contend was an improper firing. The case names as defendants the Justice Department, the FBI, and the inspector general's office. In a May 3 email to the FBI's Office of Professional Responsibility, Snyder requested records about the FBI's "Offense Codes," media relations policy, and any other manuals about internal investigations and discipline that might relate to McCabe's firing, but the FBI and DOJ lawyers turned down the request.

A spokeswoman for the DOJ declined to comment, and a spokesman for the watchdog office did not immediately return messages seeking comment. The lawsuit also comes just days ahead of a Justice Department inspector general report expected to criticize senior FBI officials, including McCabe, for their actions during the Hillary Clinton email investigation. McCabe's lawyers express their intent to continue pursuing legal avenues to address what they view as an unjust dismissal.

HONG KONG (AP) — Seven Hong Kong pro-democracy activists pleaded guilty Thursday to organizing and inciting others to take part in an unauthorized assembly held in 2019, local media reported. The activists appearing in court included Raphael Wong, the former chairman of the League of Social Democrats political party, and Figo Chan, who led the Civil Human Rights Front, a now-disbanded group that organized protests.

"I was protesting based on the principle of civil disobedience. One of the key elements of civil disobedience is to accept the charges. So that is what we are going to do later, to plead guilty," Wong said Thursday ahead of the proceedings. He added, "Another key element is that the people carrying out civil disobedience actions know being jailed is just part of the process. We are not worried about being jailed. Instead, we hope we can achieve democracy after this process."

The activists are the latest to appear in court for charges related to the 2019 anti-government protests that roiled the semiautonomous Chinese territory. The protests were sparked by concerns that Beijing was infringing on the freedoms promised to the former British colony when it was handed to Chinese control in 1997. Beijing responded to the protests by imposing a strict new national security law last year that has effectively criminalized much of the opposition to the government and silenced dissent.

Most of the city’s most prominent activists, including Joshua Wong and Apple Daily founder Jimmy Lai, are currently behind bars. Many of them were prosecuted for taking part in unauthorized protests in 2019. Of the seven defendants on Thursday, only Raphael Wong was not held in custody prior to appearing in court. The other six are currently behind bars after being convicted of other offenses related to their activism.

Local news outlets Ming Pao and Stand News later reported all seven pleaded guilty.
